title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a manuscript note. It is a typescript page, p. 76 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 I ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §6.2. It has evidently been filed among the 1976 PD-de Rham notes; the neighbouring pages, on truncations τ_N and the derived functors R^nφ_{N',N}, are unrelated.

Setting.
- S is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue characteristic p.
- A_K is an abelian variety with Néron model A and dual A'.
- A_o is the special fibre and A_o^o its identity component.
- \overline{A_o} is the maximal semi-abelian subgroup of A_o^o, an extension of an abelian variety by a torus T_o.

The question is whether the Barsotti–Tate group of \overline{A_o} extends to a sub-Barsotti–Tate group F of the p-divisible group of A. Such an F would be the p-adic analogue of the fixed part T_ℓ(A)^f from 2.2.3.2.
- In the semi-stable case \overline{A_o} = A_o^o, and the answer is yes by the method of 2.2.
- In general, if a solution exists it is unique. It then satisfies the orthogonality theorem 5.2 between T_p(A_K) and T_p(A'_K), and the characterization of 5.8.

6.2.1 shows that in general no solution exists.
- Take S complete. By the Serre–Tate lifting theorem [30], existence of F is equivalent to existence of infinitesimal liftings \overline{A_n} of \overline{A_o} inside the A_n.
- Equivalently, it amounts to a smooth group scheme \overline{A} over S, an extension of an abelian scheme by a torus with special fibre \overline{A_o}, together with a formal homomorphism \hat{\overline{A}} → \hat{A} extending the inclusion on special fibres.
- If T_o = 0, this means an abelian scheme \overline{A} lifting \overline{A_o}, together with an actual homomorphism \overline{A} → A (by algebraization and the Néron property).

So it suffices to exhibit a case with T_o = 0, A_o^o non-unipotent and non-proper, and A_K simple.
- Non-unipotent with no torus means the abelian part is nonzero, so \overline{A_o} ≠ 0.
- Non-proper means dim \overline{A_o} < dim A_o.
- The generic fibre of \overline{A} → A would then map to a nonzero abelian subvariety of A_K of smaller dimension. This contradicts simplicity.
errors: No mathematical error. The step from a formal homomorphism to an algebraic homomorphism \overline{A} → A (via Grothendieck existence plus the Néron mapping property) is left implicit, but it is standard.

ideas.what: Obstruction to defining a p-adic 'fixed part' T_p(A)^f in non-semi-stable reduction, via Serre–Tate lifting
ideas.modern_name: Non-extendability of the p-divisible group of the abelian part of the Néron special fibre; p-adic fixed part
